title: Knee Arthroscopy for Meniscal Tears (Synthetic Health Plan — fictional policy)
scope: Arthroscopic partial meniscectomy or meniscal repair
notes: Curated against workstream B fixture syn_knee_arthroscopy.json (synthetic policy).

children.text: Mechanical symptoms (locking, catching or giving way) documented in the clinical record

sourceSpan.quote: The member reports mechanical symptoms of the knee, such as locking, catching, or giving way, documented in the clinical record.

present: {date}: Reports intermittent locking and catching of the right knee; McMurray positive medially.
negated: {date}: Denies locking or catching; McMurray negative.
contradicted: {date}: No mechanical symptoms; exam without joint line tenderness.
paraphrased: {date}: Knee intermittently gets stuck and has to be wiggled free; medial joint line is tender to palpation.

children.text: At least 6 weeks of conservative therapy (PT or supervised home exercise plus NSAID, activity modification or bracing) within the past 12 months

sourceSpan.quote: The member has completed at least 6 weeks of conservative therapy within the past 12 months, including physical therapy or a supervised home exercise program

children.suggestedFix: Document PT/home-exercise dates (start and end), medications or bracing tried and the response.

present: {date}: Completed 8 weeks of physical therapy (2x weekly) and meloxicam 15 mg daily with minimal improvement.
negated: {date}: Has not started physical therapy; no medications tried.
contradicted: {date}: After 3 weeks of PT, symptoms markedly improved.
paraphrased: {date}: Two months of supervised therapy and daily NSAIDs did not relieve the knee pain.

children.text: Exception: locked knee that cannot be reduced, or acute displaced bucket-handle tear on MRI

sourceSpan.quote: there is a locked knee that cannot be reduced, or an acute traumatic tear with a displaced bucket-handle fragment confirmed on MRI

present: {date}: Knee locked in 20 degrees of flexion, unable to reduce in clinic; MRI shows displaced bucket-handle fragment.

children.text: MRI within the past 6 months shows a meniscal tear that correlates with clinical findings

sourceSpan.quote: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) performed within the past 6 months demonstrates a meniscal tear that correlates with the clinical findings.

children.suggestedFix: Attach the knee MRI report (dated within 6 months) and an exam note correlating findings.

present: {date}: MRI right knee: complex tear of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus; medial joint line tenderness on exam, concordant.
contradicted: {date}: MRI right knee: menisci intact; no tear identified.
paraphrased: {date}: Knee MR imaging shows a horizontal cleavage tear of the medial meniscus posterior horn, matching the site of pain on examination.

children.text: No advanced osteoarthritis (Kellgren-Lawrence grade 3 or 4) of the affected compartment on radiographs

sourceSpan.quote: Radiographs do not demonstrate advanced osteoarthritis of the affected compartment (Kellgren-Lawrence grade 3 or 4).

children.suggestedFix: Attach weight-bearing knee radiographs with an explicit Kellgren-Lawrence grade.

present: {date}: Weight-bearing X-rays right knee: Kellgren-Lawrence grade 1, joint spaces preserved.
contradicted: {date}: Weight-bearing X-rays: Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 medial compartment osteoarthritis with bone-on-bone contact.

children.text: Functional limitation attributable to the knee documented (stairs, ambulation, work), with a validated score where available

sourceSpan.quote: A functional limitation attributable to the knee is documented, such as difficulty with stairs, ambulation, or work duties

present: {date}: KOOS function score 41; unable to climb stairs or squat at work as a warehouse associate.
paraphrased: {date}: IKDC 48; cannot kneel or use stairs at home without assistance.
